title: Paul DeDroit in Hollywood studios and Petrillo's rules
summary: DeDroit describes his brother's career as a studio player under Alfred Newman and Petrillo's work rules.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I said, no. She said, well your brother called you Simon. He says, Jewish. I said, he calls me lots of things. I said, but I'm not Jewish, you know what I mean? But he was funny. He was the best company in the world. But he used to break up that band. He's the first one that I ever heard take a half a chorus on the drums. They didn't feature the drums much in the old days, you know. No. No. But he'd play on the rim and on the floor and everything. I understand when he played first trumpet, I mean played drums at the Longstreet Symphony, he's no faker. He had to read to play with Alfred Newman, you know. Because the arrangers would play out of the orchestra. And when he played the vibraphones, he used to say, what are you trying to do? Hit the first note and the last. You know what to do. You know he'd put on all the fancy vibraphone, and all that stuff, you know. But Paul stayed with him 23 years, so he must know that he was first trumpet. And he used to go in there and listen to the music and make the cuts and get extra overtime, you know, sit there with the guy and cut. You know sometimes they have to hear the music to see if it's right. And even if there are 82 men getting 28 months in a row, Paul made tremendous money on it. Oh God. But in the beginning it was so unorganized. You couldn't go get a haircut, you didn't tell them you were in a barbershop. They could call you at any hour. So Petrillo went out there and he told them that if you don't tell the men before six o'clock today that they're going to play tomorrow, you can't have them. See? If I didn't tell you, the next session will be nine o'clock tomorrow, you didn't have to worry about it. They couldn't call you. It was all, and then they had to do things over and over. They made so many mistakes. They used to get paid twice sometimes. But it got down to where they could play for three stages at one time. Alfred Newman had three televisions on his track. And he could watch three scenes with the same music. I don't know how they did it, but it got to be, I don't know if I could play with, I told you you played with earphones. What do you call them? Earphones. Yeah. The human being didn't come.
